title: Your first session with Clio
description: Connect a model, open a repository, and ask Clio to explain how it builds and runs its tests.
author: The Clio team

title: Desktop or terminal: find your workspace
description: See both interfaces, learn how to launch them, and choose where to start your next coding session.
author: The Clio team

title: A numerical change, checked with Clio
description: Follow a temperature-conversion example through a floating-point test failure, a correction, and recorded verification.
author: The Clio team

title: Choose a model for your project
description: Connect a local server, a cloud API, or a supported subscription route, then choose models separately for conversation and delegated work.
author: The Clio team

title: Coordinate the coding agents you already use
description: Use supported coding peers for bounded assignments, distinguish managed runs from interactive handoffs, and review the results before combining them.
author: The Clio team

title: Keep a long coding task on track
description: Inspect context, preserve decisions through a handoff, and resume the correct branch without turning every past message into a current instruction.
author: The Clio team

title: Check a change against your repository
description: Declare which checks matter, run them through verification, and inspect whether passing results still match the files you are reviewing.
author: The Clio team

title: Add skills and plugins deliberately
description: Preview a project-scoped skill or plugin, inspect its package pin, and load the resources your task needs without treating an installation as a permission grant.
author: The Clio team

title: Work from a laptop with remote workers
description: Use a local Clio session to coordinate SSH workers when your machines share the required project path, runtime version, and approved access.
author: The Clio team
